en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Tuvaṭṭa, 36.
The Training Rule on Socializing.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the nun Caṇḍakāḷī was living in close association with householders and the sons of householders.
Those nuns who were few in desires... [as before] ...were indignant, complained, and grumbled, saying:
"How can the noble lady Caṇḍakāḷī live in close association with householders and the sons of householders?"... [as before] ...
“Is it true, monks, that the nun Caṇḍakāḷī lives in association with householders and even with the sons of householders?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī live in association with householders and even with the sons of householders?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: ‘If a bhikkhunī should live in association with a householder or with the son of a householder, there is an offense of expiation.’”
“Whatever nun should live in association with a householder or a householder’s son, that nun should be addressed by the nuns thus:
‘Venerable lady, do not live in association with a householder or a householder’s son. Venerable lady, stay apart; the Saṅgha praises seclusion for you, sister.
If that nun, being so addressed by the nuns, should persist as before, that nun is to be formally admonished by the nuns up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that behavior.
“If, after being exhorted up to three times, she should relinquish it, that is good; if she should not relinquish it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“But which [nun]? means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so on].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"In association" (saṃsaṭṭhā) means:
They associate with him in ways that are unwholesome through body and speech.
A "householder" is anyone who dwells in a home.
"Gahapatiputta" refers to any sons or brothers.
"That bhikkhunī" refers to [the one previously mentioned].
That nun who is associating.
"By the nuns" means by other nuns. Those who see her or hear of it should say to her:
“Venerable lady, do not dwell in association with householders or the sons of householders.
Venerable lady, live in seclusion;
the Saṅgha praises seclusion for you, sister.”
A second time she should be told.
A third time she should be told.
If she relinquishes it, that is good.
If she does not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Having heard [the charge], if they do not speak, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
That bhikkhunī should be dragged even into the midst of the Saṅgha and addressed thus:
“Venerable lady, do not dwell in association with householders or the sons of householders.
Dwell in seclusion, venerable lady;
the Saṅgha praises seclusion for you, sister.”
It should be said a second time.
It should be said a third time.
If she relinquishes it, that is good.
If she does not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
That bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished.
"And thus, monks, is she to be formally admonished: [insert formal admonition here]."
The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and experienced bhikkhunī:
“Let the noble Saṅgha listen to me.
This bhikkhunī named so-and-so lives in association with householders and the sons of householders.”
She does not relinquish that matter.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha formally admonish the bhikkhunī named so-and-so for the relinquishing of that matter.
This is the motion.
"Venerable ladies, let the Saṅgha hear me.
This nun, so-and-so, lives in association with both householders and the sons of householders;
she does not relinquish that course of conduct."
The Sangha exhorts the bhikkhunī named so-and-so for the relinquishing of that matter.
Whichever noble lady approves of the exhortation of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so for the relinquishing of that matter, let her be silent;
whichever does not approve, let her speak.
A second time I speak this matter...
A third time I speak this matter...
The Saṅgha has formally admonished the bhikkhunī named so-and-so for the relinquishing of that matter.
“The Saṅgha consents, therefore it is silent; thus do I understand this.
There is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) for the motion;
there are offenses of wrong-doing for the two formal proclamations.
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation (kammavācā), there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If it is a legitimate legal act (dhammakamma) and one perceives it as such, yet does not relinquish [the position], there is an offense of expiation.
If it is a legitimate legal act and one is in doubt, yet does not relinquish [the position], there is an offense of expiation.

If it is a legitimate legal act (*dhammakamma*) and one perceives it as an illegitimate legal act (*adhammakamma*), yet does not relinquish [the action], there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
If it is an illegitimate legal act and one perceives it as a legitimate legal act, there is an offense of wrongdoing (*dukkaṭa*).
If it is an illegitimate legal act and one is doubtful [about its legitimacy], there is an offense of wrongdoing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and she perceives it as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if she does not admonish [the monks].
For one who relinquishes it,
for one who is insane,
and for one who is a first-time offender.
The sixth training rule is finished.
